### Building a New PC – A Step‑by‑Step Guide Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough. Feel free to skip sections you already know, but keep the order for safety and best results. | # | Step | What to Do | Tips | |---|------|------------|------| | 1 | **Plan & Budget** | • Decide what you’ll use it for (gaming, video editing, office, etc.).
• Set a budget (CPU, GPU, RAM, storage, case, PSU, peripherals). | Use online PC builders (PCPartPicker, BuildMyPC) to check compatibility and prices. | | 2 | **Gather Tools & Workspace** | • Phillips screwdriver (magnetic tip helps).
• Anti‑static wrist strap or mat.
• Clean, flat surface. | Keep the case open and components on a static‑free surface. | | 3 | **Choose Components** | • **CPU** (Intel/AMD).
• **Motherboard** (socket, chipset, form factor).
• **RAM** (DDR4/DDR5, speed, capacity).
• **GPU** (if not integrated).
• **Storage** (SSD/HDD, NVMe vs SATA).
• **Power Supply** (wattage, 80+ rating).
• **Case** (ATX, mATX, mini‑ITX).
• **Cooling** (stock cooler, aftermarket air, or AIO liquid). | Check compatibility lists (e.g., CPU socket vs motherboard). | | 4 | **Prepare the Case** | • Remove side panels.
• Install standoffs for the motherboard (usually pre‑installed). | Some cases have pre‑installed standoffs; others need you to screw them in. | | 5 | **Install the CPU** | • Open the CPU socket latch.
• Align the CPU (gold triangle) with the socket.
• Gently place it, then lock the latch. | Don’t force; the socket will guide it. | | 6 | **Apply Thermal Paste & Install Cooler** | • If using an aftermarket cooler, apply a pea‑size amount of thermal paste on the CPU.
• Mount the cooler according to its instructions. | Many stock coolers come with pre‑applied paste. | | 7 | **Insert RAM** | • Open the RAM slots’ clips.
• Align the notch on the RAM stick with the slot.
• Push firmly until the clips click. | Install in pairs for dual‑channel mode. | | 8 | **Mount the Motherboard** | • Align the motherboard with the I/O shield and standoffs.
• Screw it down. | Double‑check that all ports line up with the case cutouts. | | 9 | **Install Storage** | • Mount SSD/HDD in the drive bays or M.2 slot.
• Secure with screws or clips. | NVMe drives go into the M.2 slot; SATA drives need a 2.5” bay or 3.5” bay. | | 10 | **Install Power Supply** | • Place PSU in the case (bottom or top, depending on case).
• Secure with screws.
• Route cables to the motherboard, GPU, drives, and case fans. | Keep cables tidy; use cable ties or Velcro straps. | | 11 | **Install GPU (if applicable)** | • Remove the appropriate expansion slot covers on the case.
• Insert GPU into the top PCI‑e x16 slot.
• Secure with screws. | Connect any required PCI‑e power connectors from the PSU. | | 12 | **Connect Case Fans & Front Panel** | • Connect case fans to the motherboard fan headers or PSU.
• Connect front panel connectors (USB, audio, power button, reset button) to the motherboard. | Refer to the motherboard manual for exact pin layout. | | 13 | **Cable Management** | • Route cables behind the motherboard tray.
• Use cable ties to bundle and secure. | Good airflow and easier future upgrades. | | 14 | **First Boot** | • Connect a monitor, keyboard, and mouse.
• Power on the system.
• Enter BIOS/UEFI (usually F2, Del, or Esc). | Check that all components are detected (CPU, RAM, GPU, storage). | | 15 | **Install Operating System** | • Create a bootable USB with Windows, Linux, etc.
• Boot from USB and install OS. | Install drivers after OS installation (GPU, chipset, Wi‑Fi). | | 16 | **Update & Test** | • Install all drivers and firmware updates.
• Run stress tests (Prime95, 3DMark, CrystalDiskMark). | Monitor temperatures and voltages to ensure stability. | | 17 | **Final Touches** | • Replace side panels.
• Adjust fan curves for noise/temperature balance.
• Install additional peripherals (keyboard, mouse, speakers). | Keep the system in a dust‑free environment. | --- #### Quick Checklist - [ ] CPU + cooler installed - [ ] RAM seated - [ ] Motherboard mounted - [ ] PSU installed - [ ] GPU installed (if needed) - [ ] Storage installed - [ ] Cables connected & managed - [ ] BIOS settings checked - [ ] OS installed - [ ] Drivers updated - [ ] Stress test passed --- #### Common Pitfalls & Fixes | Issue | Likely Cause | Fix | |-------|--------------|-----| | System won’t power on | PSU not connected or switched off | Verify PSU switch, check all power cables | | No display | GPU not seated or power connector missing | Re‑seat GPU, connect PCI‑e power | | Overheating | Poor airflow or inadequate cooling | Add case fans, improve cable routing | | BIOS not detecting RAM | Incorrect slot or faulty stick | Try different slot, test RAM in another system | | Blue screen after OS install | Driver conflict or faulty hardware | Update drivers, run memory test (MemTest86) | --- #### Resources - **PCPartPicker** – component compatibility checker and price comparison. - **YouTube** – “How to Build a PC” series (e.g., Linus Tech Tips, JayzTwoCents). - **Manufacturer manuals** – always refer to the motherboard, PSU, and case manuals for specific instructions. Happy building! If you hit a snag, let me know which step and I’ll help troubleshoot.
message.reasoning: User asks "How to build a new PC?" They want instructions. We can provide a step-by-step guide. No function call needed.
